title: Clusters formation and fragmentation of nitromethane at 266 nm
author: Martínez, Guerrero, et al.

steps.title: Prepare nitromethane sample
steps.instruction: Use liquid nitromethane (Sigma‑Aldrich, ~99 % purity). Heat the sample to a constant 28 °C and load it into the pulse valve for gas‑phase introduction.

steps.title: Assemble supersonic molecular beam
steps.instruction: Install a pulsed valve followed by a 10 cm stainless‑steel extension ending in a 2 mm conical tip; position the extension 10 mm upstream of a skimmer and maintain a collision‑free chamber.

steps.title: Operate valve and maintain vacuum
steps.instruction: Open the valve for 175 µs to generate the beam while keeping the ionization chamber at 2 × 10⁻⁶ torr (open valve) and a base pressure of 10⁻⁸ torr using two turbo‑molecular pumps (Pfeiffer Vacuum and Agilent).

steps.title: Focus laser into interaction region
steps.instruction: Direct a vertically polarized Gaussian laser beam through a 15 cm focal‑length lens to obtain an 80.0 µm spot at the interaction zone; adjust the pulse energy to achieve intensities between 1 × 10⁹ and 1 × 10¹⁰ W·cm⁻².

steps.title: Align beam‑laser intersection
steps.instruction: Arrange the laser and the molecular beam to intersect at 90° inside the interaction region, which is bounded by two polarized electrodes spaced 6 mm apart and fitted with a circular mesh (90 % transparency, 1 cm diameter).

steps.title: Apply extraction voltage
steps.instruction: Apply a 1.5 keV extraction voltage to the electrodes to accelerate the positive fragments produced by the nanosecond laser pulse into the field‑free region of the reflectron‑time‑of‑flight (R‑TOF) mass spectrometer.

steps.title: Detect ions with MCP detector
steps.instruction: After the drift zone, guide the ions to a 25 mm dual Chevron microchannel plate (MCP) detector; route the MCP output to a VT‑120 fast preamplifier (ORTEC) and a 9308 picosecond time analyzer (ORTEC).

steps.title: Configure data acquisition electronics
steps.instruction: Set the time‑of‑flight analyzer to scan from 400 ns up to 2.7 years using approximately 65 000 channels; note that the MCP response is on the order of nanoseconds, the single‑charge time interval Δ(1,2) = 0.95 × 10⁻⁶ s, the 1 amu vs 2 amu arrival‑time difference ≈ 10⁻⁶ s, detection time ≈ 10⁻⁹ s, and electronic response ≈ 10⁻¹² s.

steps.title: Collect and process mass spectra
steps.instruction: Use a computer running PTA‑32 (ORTEC) software to record ion arrival times, generate fragment spectra, and assign each peak to its corresponding nitromethane fragment.
